messages:
Alex: Heads-up — saw a paging spike on us-east-1-prod at 03:12 UTC, ~2x baseline. Appears correlated with a set of models that bumped host staging on gpu-pool-7. I grabbed a few samples and logs.
Maya: ugh. any infra/runtime deploys rolled in the last 24h?
Alex: No infra deploys. Runtime rolled a small kv-cache eviction tweak yesterday evening. Snippet from runtime log: ```evict: policy=age_based batch_size=64 delay_ms=0``` — noticed a lot more aggressive evicts around the spike.
Simon: can you paste the paging counters? wall of numbers helps.
Alex: Per-host page faults/sec: host-37: 420 -> 850, host-42: 380 -> 760. KV miss rate +3x. NVMe reads on /dev/nvme1 spiked. ps/top shows copier threads pegged at ~90% CPU.
infra-bot: alert: paging_spike_us-east-1 at 2025-03-14T03:12:14Z — severity: warning — affected_hosts=12
Jess: Could batch sizing be interacting with eviction? We bumped max_batch_tokens to 8192 in model-configs last week.
Maya: If request batches are larger we may be touching bigger contiguous working sets. Combine that with more aggressive kv-evict and you get thrashing + fragmentation -> more host reads.
Alex: Reproduced locally on staging: ran ./scripts/hotset_sim.sh --batch=8192 --clients=8 and saw resident set oscillate and host reads jump. Local log excerpt: ```host_read_ms=1200 avg_page_faults=650 sample=2025-03-14T03:11:58Z```.
Liam: two quick mitigations: rollback the kv-cache eviction tweak (low blast radius), or add a per-request batch throttle (needs SDK/serving change). Which is faster to push?
Simon: rollback eviction tweak first — easier to revert and monitor. Throttle needs coordination and a release window.
Maya: I'll open a rollback PR and canary it to 10% of gpu-pool-7 within the hour. Also will add a short delay on evict loop to smooth spikes.
Jess: I'll add an alert rule: page_faults/s > 300 sustained for 2m and a dashboard row for host_read_latency and nvme_iops. Also adding a tenant-level hotset chart.
Alex: I'll collect per-tenant traces and hotset maps (pmap + slab stats) and post them. For now we're prioritizing rollback + canary. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Maya: ETA for rollback PR in 15m, will post links here.
Simon: After canary, let's run the synthetic high-batch workload against canary machines to validate.
Liam: I can coordinate the synthetic run and record traces.
Jess: Alert/graphing changes pushed to staging. Will prod them after canary.
Alex: Dumped pmap + /proc/slabinfo for host-37 and uploaded to the runbook. Key observation: fragmented host allocations, many small slab allocations around the same hotset.
Maya: That matches theory — fragmentation + aggressive eviction -> more page churn. Long-term we should consider a soft-residency window (keep small hot prefix pinned) or prefault heuristics for large batches.
Simon: Agree. Add to the backlog: (1) soft-residency policy RFC, (2) batch-aware prefetch/prefaulting, (3) eviction pacing heuristics.
Alex: Made the three-ticket stub and linked to this thread.
infra-bot: deploy: rollback-evict-tweak started @ 2025-03-14T03:48:02Z — target=10%gpu-pool-7
Jess: monitoring shows page_faults/s trending down on canary hosts. Will update in 10m.
Alex: Nice, keep watching nvme_iops and kv-miss-rate. We'll regroup after canary completes.
Maya: Thanks team. Follow-up sync in #eng-runtime after canary if stable.
